args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). Per the platform runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and is not deployed. The staging build v2.3.1-rc is also marked unhealthy. Next steps: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any re-release. Re-deploying v2.3.1 would require change-manager approval because it has never been healthy in production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with a 0.18 error rate. I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. It is now running in us-east, us-west and eu-west.
- **Result:** The service reports healthy, with an error rate of 0.002.
- **Approval:** v2.3.0 has a healthy production history, so the change-manager approval policy did not apply.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the post-rollback status. It also notes that v2.3.1 needs investigation and that re-deploying it would need change-manager approval, since it has never been healthy in production.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 is the unhealthy one currently running in all three regions. v2.3.0 has a healthy production history, so the change-manager approval policy doesn't apply. Rolling back now.
